tagline: Turn vague requests into answerable decision questions, plan the analysis, and review analyses by people and assistants by consequence
description: Participants practise the work before and after an analysis, using requests from Ghadeer Water Company, a fictional water utility. They turn vague requests into decision questions with an estimand, a metric and a decision rule, interview a role-played manager, use domain knowledge of metering, billing and repair to see where the data mislead, and test whether data and deadline make the question answerable. They then review analyses by peers and by an assistant and write review notes ranked by consequence. Metric definition is DS-307; team review standards are DS-407.
audience: Practitioners. Data scientists and analysts who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: an analysis they framed, carried out and explained to a stakeholder.
prerequisites: DS-204 Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation
Has completed at least one analysis for a stakeholder
Reads a notebook in Python or R and reruns it

Setup: a laptop processor with uv, or Google Colab. Nothing downloads a model; a free hosted model key is optional (every assistant cell has a stand-in). Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

case_study.name: Ghadeer Water Company
case_study.summary: Ghadeer Water Company is a fictional water utility with six districts whose managers send vague requests about water loss, leak repair, billing and complaints. Participants frame those requests with an estimand and a decision rule, interview a role-played operations manager and metering engineer, map how meter reads become bills, stress-test the water-loss and customer-service metric tree, write and attack analysis plans, and review three seeded-flaw analyses, one written by the assistant Sareea. The capstone moves to a second case, the Building Permits Department of Hima Municipality and its permits backlog. All data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed.
